findings.title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED slug logic
findings.body: In create.handler.ts the spread was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `requestedSlug` similarly. The old code included `slug` when billing was disabled and `requestedSlug` when enabled; the new code does the opposite. As a result organizations will be created with the wrong slug/requestedSlug fields, breaking org creation/routing. This change is unrelated to destinationCalendar and inverts behavior.

findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty on Meet fallback
findings.body: In EventManager.ts `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` can be undefined when there is no destination calendar, but the next line does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. Any booking without a destinationCalendar with location Google Meet will throw TypeError and fail booking creation. It must be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback calendarId can never resolve
findings.body: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy. Searching for `externalId === externalCalendarId` when externalCalendarId is null/undefined will never match, so calendarId becomes undefined and `calendar.events.update` is called with undefined calendarId. Reschedule/update without an explicit externalCalendarId will fail instead of falling back to the first destinationCalendar.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback calendarId can never resolve
findings.body: In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy. That predicate can never be true, so calendarId is undefined and the code falls back to "primary" even when the event has an explicit destinationCalendar. Deleting collective/secondary-host events can hit the wrong calendar or silently succeed on primary without deleting the real event.

findings.title: Collective team calendars dropped when organizer has no calendar
findings.body: In handleNewBooking.ts evt.destinationCalendar is built as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [...] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : null`, then later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` for COLLECTIVE. When both are missing the value is null, the optional push is a no-op, so teamDestinationCalendars collected from hosts are lost. EventManager then sees no destinationCalendar and falls back to a single calendar, so additional collective hosts never get calendar events. Initialize to [] instead of null.

findings.title: Webhook expectations left as null after type changed to array
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar was changed from single object/null to array, and one BOOKING_REJECTED expectation was updated to `[]`. The BOOKING_CREATED expectation at line 119 and BOOKING_REQUESTED at line 373 still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. The webhook payload will now be `[]`, so those e2e assertions will fail and the breaking API contract change (null -> []) is not consistently documented/tested.
